Doesn’t make it better but there is a big difference between a tactical nuclear weapon built for precision and an actual nuclear weapon that’s aimed at maximum casualties. 

The primary difference between a tactical nuclear weapon and a strategic nuclear weapon is their intended target and scope.

Tactical nuclear weapons are designed for specific battlefield use. They have a shorter range and generally lower explosive power, meant to destroy localized targets like troop columns, military bases, or naval fleets without destroying the surrounding region.

Strategic nuclear weapons are designed to win wars by targeting an enemy nation's entire infrastructure, major cities, and military centers

At six months post election day, the S&P has been higher for every single midterm since 1950. 

Average gain of 13.8% six months out, with a 100% hit rate across 19 midterms. [link]

Markets are heading into their strongest seasonal period of the year:

Since 1980, the S&P 500 has rallied +2.1% on average in November, making it the strongest month of the year.

Over this period, positive returns occurred 74% of the time, the best hit rate of any month.

Furthermore, the S&P 500 has gained +1.6% on average in November since 1964, with positive returns occurring 69% of the time.

The highest November return during this period was +10.8%, recorded in 2020.

During midterm years, November has averaged +2.7% since 1950, with a 78.9% win rate.

History points to a strong month ahead.
